traits.note: FNA vol. 28, Rosulabryum (Spence; efloras, read 2026-11-05): plants in open to dense low turfs, green to red-green; stems 0.3-6 cm, usually rosulate; leaves contorted to spirally twisted around the stem when dry; costa usually excurrent in an awn; dioicous mostly; seta straight; capsule nutant to inclined, 2-6 mm. Typical values are R. capillare (Bryum capillare; same volume): small, bright green; stems 0.5-1.5 cm; leaves spirally twisted around the stem dry, obovate, 0.5-2.5 mm, costa long-excurrent, awn sometimes hyaline; capsule inclined, red-brown, cylindric, 3-5 mm; moist shaded soil, soil banks, rotting wood. Bryophytes at Oregon State, rooftop study (nine Willamette Valley roofs; read 2026-11-05 as summarised in a search, the site itself blocked here): Dicranoweisia cirrata very abundant (45% occurrence), Bryum capillare abundant (33%), Racomitrium canescens var. ericoides abundant but infrequent (11%), able to form large mats; Dicranoweisia and Bryum capillare the only two species found on cedar shakes; most roofs had fewer than four species.

traits.leaf_shape.note: FNA vol. 28, Rosulabryum capillare (efloras, read 2026-11-05): leaves obovate, weakly concave, apex acute, costa long-excurrent.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Obovate leaves about two fifths as wide as long.

traits.hair_point_length_m.note: FNA: costa long-excurrent, the awn only sometimes hyaline; the colourless part drawn short, so the turf reads bright green, not silvery.

traits.seta_length_m.note: FNA gives no seta length for R. capillare; 1-3 cm as in Bryum (seta 1-2 cm in B. argenteum). Check against a measured flora.

traits.substrates.note: FNA's soil and rotting wood, roofs and cedar shakes from OSU's survey, bark as in European floras (general bryological knowledge).

traits.light.note: FNA's moist shaded soil: shade to part shade.

traits.substrate_reaction.note: FNA's rotting wood and OSU's cedar shakes; FNA names no calcareous habitat for R. capillare.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: As Bryum; to check against Glime, Bryophyte Ecology.

traits.capsule_shape.note: FNA vol. 28, Rosulabryum capillare: capsule cylindric to elongate-pyriform. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.operculum_form.note: FNA vol. 28, Rosulabryum: operculum short-conic to umbonate. (efloras, read 2026-11-05)

traits.leaf_colour.note: Hue measured: imagekit run moss-colour-2026-11-05 on batch moss-pnw-2026-11-05 (iNaturalist research-grade photos from Washington, about 20 a taxon, script moss_colour.py): the median linear r/g and b/g of the moss pixels (R. capillare r/g 0.90, b/g 0.12, masked median only). Photos are exposed brighter than moss is, so only the hue is taken from them; the brightness is a green reflectance of 0.13, a lit leaf's, just above the 0.05-0.11 moss canopies reflect in the visible (Lovelock and Robinson 2002, Plant Cell Environ. 25: 1239, Antarctic Grimmia; moss biocrust albedo about 0.11 against 0.20 for bare soil, Sci. Total Environ. 2020), the canopy's own shade darkening the shell further.
